I'm 67 this year. I've been farming these 16 mu for 20 years now — took them over from my brother when he went to work in the city. My son is in Shijiazhuang at a construction site, and my daughter-in-law works at a garment factory there. They send money home, which helps, but I still have to watch every yuan. My wife and I do most of the farm work, though my son comes back for wheat harvest and cotton picking when he can.

I have 9 mu that I do wheat-maize double cropping on, and the other 7 mu is cotton. That's how I've done it for years. The cotton land is in the south part of my plot, better drained.

**Winter wheat** — I planted it last October, early, before the National Day holiday even ended. The variety is Jimai 22, same as my neighbor Lao Wang uses. I already put down base fertilizer at planting — about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's March and the wheat is greening up. The stand looks okay, not great but okay. I'm going to topdress urea at jointing in about two weeks, around 20 jin per mu. Last year I skimped a bit, only did 15 jin, and the yield dropped to maybe 400 kg/mu. Not making that mistake again. I'll irrigate twice more — once at jointing and once at grain filling. If it rains in May maybe I skip the last one. I sprayed herbicide already in early spring, and if I see aphids I'll spray insecticide. I'm hoping for 430 kg/mu, maybe 450 if the weather cooperates.

**Summer maize** — This is the busy time. As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I have to get the maize in the ground within three or four days, no time to plow properly. I hire a combine for the wheat, then I plant maize direct with a hand planter. I always buy hybrid seed, new seed every year — I don't save maize seed, that's just asking for trouble. It's about 55 yuan per mu for the seed. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 50 jin per mu, and then at big trumpet stage in July I topdress with another 30 jin of urea. I'll irrigate twice if July is dry. I don't worry too much about maize pests unless I see borers. Last year I got 480 kg/mu. I'll be happy with 460 this year.

**Cotton** — I plant in late April. Cotton needs more work. I plow that 7 mu in early April, then harrow it fine. I use about 1.5 kg of seed per mu, improved variety, costs about 35 yuan. For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer before planting, about 45 jin per mu, and then at flowering in July I put down 25 jin of urea. Cotton needs water but not too much — twice is enough unless it's very dry in August. The real cost is pesticide. I have to spray for bollworm three or four times, and herbicide once. That adds up. Cotton picking is the hardest part. My whole family works on it — my wife, me, my daughter-in-law when she's not at the factory, and we hire local women to help pick. We pay them by the jin. I'm hoping for about 260 kg per mu of seed cotton. The price last year was decent, so if the bollworms don't get bad, it should be alright.

I have to be careful with cash. Even though my son sends money, I can't spend it all on the farm — we might need it for medicine or something. Total costs for inputs this year — seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation pumping, hired picking labor — I reckon about 7,800 yuan. Maybe 8,000 if I have to spray more. It's a lot, but if both crops do okay, we'll cover it and have enough left for the year.
